data.gender_notes: Andrews is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Andrews is derived from the Greek name Andreas, which means man or masculine. In the New Testament, Saint Andrew was the brother of Saint Peter and the first disciple to follow Jesus. The name Andrews carries the meaning “Man, masculine” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Andrews usually hope their child will grow to embody man, masculine and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name representing strength, courage, and faith in God.
data.etymology: Andrews belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Man, masculine.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Andrews total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.
data.cultural_impact: The name Andrews has been carried by numerous influential figures in various fields, including politics, arts, and religion. In the Catholic Church, many saints and blessed have carried this name in recognition of Saint Andrew's role as an early disciple and leader in the Christian faith. In Anglo-Saxon England, the name Andrew was Anglicized to Andrews, and it became a common surname.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Andrews holds rich spiritual meaning, as it pays homage to the legendary early Christian disciple, Saint Andrew. Aside from being a symbol of faith and devotion, the name Andrews signifies a deep connection to the Christian religious heritage. The name also conveys a sense of strength, masculinity, and leadership, reminding us of the bravery and determination display by Saint Andrew in spreading the message of love, hope, and faith.
